_ownerRuling: Owner ruling 2026-09-02, verbatim: "Correct it the best way you can. making this decision but the lens is that we want them to unlocka few items that can go in the quick swap bar fast, why because our retention number is very low and people are not returning" -- RESOLVED as follows. (1) 'tier' in this file is a COST/POWER BAND, not a prerequisite depth: cost == tierCosts[tier] on ALL 83 nodes, and the node id itself encodes the tier (<hero>.t<tier>n<slot>, branch nodes s/b). Re-labelling 'tier' to match graph depth was therefore REJECTED - it would desync every relabelled id from its own tier (ids are live save keys and cannot be renamed to follow), and it would RAISE the cost of the cheap shallow nodes (mage.t1n4, mage.t1n5) that the retention lens actually wants, or force cost overrides that break the one invariant currently holding perfectly. Knight also has depth-5 chains against 4 tiers, so a depth==tier mapping is not even expressible. Tier is consumed ONLY for capstone detection (tier4), track reading order, and a fallback y when the lattice solver fails - never for cost and never for gating. (2) The REAL retention defect was the mage's distance to a hot-swap-bar ability: knight 2 points, ranger 1 point, mage 3 points. An attempt to fix the mage by swapping the graph seats of mage.t2n5 (Blink Mastery) and mage.t1n3 (Warded Flesh) was made and then REVERTED the same day - see item (6). The mage remains at 3. (3) NOTE for the record: the SHARED universal strip (shared.n9 Arcane Bolt / n10 Mend / n11 Dash) is cost 1, no prerequisites, ungated, and available to EVERY hero - so a player's very FIRST Wisdom point already buys a castable for all three classes today. The per-class numbers above are the class-tree path only. (4) SECOND PASS, owner-approved 2026-09-02 under the same verbatim lens ("we want them to unlocka few items that can go in the quick swap bar fast, why because our retention number is very low and people are not returning"): the KNIGHT was taken from 2 points to 1 by swapping the graph seats of knight.t1n1 (Iron Resolve, stat) and knight.t1n2 (Thunderbolt, skill). Both are tier1/cost1, so the swap is COST-NEUTRAL and TIER-NEUTRAL - see the _note on each of the six touched nodes. The knight is the V1 north-star hero (only KNIGHT talent effects are wired at runtime), so this is the highest-retention-leverage edit in the file. Final class-tree points-to-first-bar-ability: knight 1, ranger 1, mage 3, shared 1. (5) RULED AND CLOSED, do not re-litigate: the four mage-pool abilities with no talent node granting them (mage.frost-nova, mage.heal, mage.meteor, mage.thunder) are deliberately left alone; they are granted by Cathedral of Magic tiers. (6) THE MAGE PROMOTION WAS REVERTED, 2026-09-02, owner ruling "Revert the mage, keep the knight." TWO OF THE OWNER'S OWN RULINGS COLLIDED and the older one wins. The 2026-08-16 base-row law (owner, verbatim: "common or specialty should still start from a few simple then really refine to the playstyle of the user") is pinned by Assets/Editor/Regression/TalentTreeShapeRegression.cs rule 2 [base]: the bottom row holds at most three nodes, every one a ROOT, and every one priced at the tree's CHEAPEST cost - a base is the simple entry-level pick, never a mid-tier node dragged down. Promoting 2-cost Blink Mastery onto the mage base row while the mage still has 1-cost tier1 nodes violates that law, and the regression failed it: "[base] bottom-row node 'mage.t2n5' costs 2 while 'mage' has a 1-cost tier". The collision hits the MAGE ONLY, because the mage is the one class with no cost-1 castable to promote - the knight swap satisfies BOTH laws (Thunderbolt is tier1/cost1) and STANDS. The mage's real fix is DESIGN work - authoring a cost-1 castable base node for the mage - not a seat shuffle, and not loosening the oracle (the owner declined to loosen it). Until that design work happens the mage is 3 points in-tree and relies on the shared strip's Arcane Bolt on turn one. (7) WO-1306, RESOLVED 2026-09-02 - THE MAGE DESIGN WORK IS DONE AND THE MAGE IS NOW 1 POINT. Owner ruling: MIRROR THE KNIGHT - the mage's first talent point buys a CASTABLE, not a passive stat - refined the same evening by a second verbatim ruling, "the blm needs to get some healing , like drain to stay balanced (early)". mage.t1n3 (Warded Flesh -> 'Siphon Ward') keeps its id, tier, slot, cost 1, iconPath, x/y and empty prerequisites - so it is STILL a cheapest-cost ROOT on the bottom row and the 2026-08-16 base-row law of item (6) is satisfied WITHOUT being loosened, which is precisely what the reverted Blink Mastery promotion could not do. Only kind (stat -> skill) and abilityId changed, the same kind=skill+abilityId+stat-payload shape mage.t2n5 already uses in this tree, so the node's +20% max HP is KEPT rather than traded for the spell. The spell is mage.siphon (classes.mage-skills in abilities.json), effect 'drainshot' - the SHIPPED HeroAbilities.ResolveDrainshot that mage.drain and ranger.healing-shot already run, NOT a second healing mechanism - and every one of its numbers is copied verbatim from mage.drain, so no new balance point was invented. A distinct id rather than granting mage.drain itself because mage.drain is a DEFAULT the mage can already press on turn zero: granting it would satisfy the metric while giving the player nothing new to press, and the knight's first point buys a spell that is NOT in his stock kit. The drain RETURN RATE is remote-tunable per the owner's follow-up ruling "be smart, dont make it need a code change, make it tweakable from a db call": combat.drainReturnPct, an integer percent, shipping default 100 = today's behaviour exactly (docs/PROD022_TUNABLE_FLAGS.md). Final class-tree points-to-first-bar-ability: knight 1, ranger 1, mage 1, shared 1. Item (2)'s 'the mage remains at 3' and item (6)'s 'until that design work happens' are both now HISTORY - they are left standing because they record why the reverted shuffle was wrong, not because the mage is still at 3.
_comment: v2 canonical talent design (TALENT_ICON_ATLAS_SPEC_2026-06-27) + WO-676 strategic branches: knight = 32 nodes across three branches — WAR (hero combat; the legacy 20 + Venombrand, branch key absent = war), STEWARD (economy, 6 nodes, ids knight.s*), BULWARK (defensive structures, 5 nodes, ids knight.b*) — plus 8+3 Shared Universal. Node id = <hero>.t<tier>n<slot> (branch nodes: s/b prefix); iconPath = Talents/<hero>/<hero>_NN (NN 21-32 = WO-676 art follow-up, sprites pending). Prereq = same-slot tier below / same-branch chain. ALL THREE heroes stored (canonical); only KNIGHT effects are wired for V1 (solo Knight north star) — mage/ranger load as data+icons, effects no-op until V2. Ally-dependent Knight effects are no-op in solo V1 (any self-portion applies) and tagged '(allies — V2)'; '(... — V-later)' marks a behavioural handler not yet built. STEWARD/BULWARK effect types are summed by HeroTalentModifiers (HeroTalentEffectTypes consts); their consumer reads land in lanes A1/A2 (WO-676 §A).

mage._comment: WO-861 A1 (owner-approved 2026-08-02) — Thrain, the ranged glass cannon. Four branches: MANA CONSERVATION + RECOVERY (Mana Flow, Aether Surge, Manaweave, Aether Form, Eternal Arcana — mana IS the survival mechanic) — SPELL POWER (Arcane Focus, Flame Mastery, Runic Overload, Aetherweaver Ascension) — SURVIVABILITY (Warded Flesh +20% HP, Blink Mastery +15% HP, Arcane Shield strengthens the Shell) — LEARNABLE SPELLS (mage.void-rift, mage.cataclysm, mage.blink, mage.manaweave; mage.frost-nova + mage.arcane-bolt are unlocked by the Cathedral of Magic instead, per A3). Node ids, tiers, slots, costs, icons and the prerequisite graph are UNCHANGED so no save-side unlock is orphaned. (A 2026-09-02 reversal of the SURVIVABILITY branch was attempted and REVERTED the same day for violating the 2026-08-16 base-row law; see the top-level _ownerRuling item (6). The branch reads Warded Flesh -> Arcane Shield -> Blink Mastery, as originally authored.) WO-1306, 2026-09-02: the SURVIVABILITY branch's ROOT is re-authored - same seat, same 1-cost, same graph - from the passive 'Warded Flesh' into 'Siphon Ward', a kind=skill node that grants the drainshot spell mage.siphon AND still carries the +20% max HP. The branch now reads Siphon Ward -> Arcane Shield -> Blink Mastery, and the mage's FIRST Wisdom point buys a castable that sustains (owner: "the blm needs to get some healing , like drain to stay balanced (early)"). Slug stays 'mage'; art sheet = Wizard.

nodes._note: WO-1306 (owner ruling 2026-09-02) - THE MAGE'S FIRST TALENT POINT NOW BUYS A CASTABLE, mirroring the knight (commit 02f9b8a4f). Owner, verbatim: "the blm needs to get some healing , like drain to stay balanced (early)", under the retention lens "we want them to unlocka few items that can go in the quick swap bar fast, why because our retention number is very low and people are not returning". The mage was the ONE class at 3 points to its first bar-equippable ability (knight 1, ranger 1, shared 1), and it was the one class with no cost-1 castable to promote - so the WO-1306 fix is DESIGN, changing what a base node DOES, not where it sits. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: id, tier, slot, cost, iconPath, x, y and prerequisites are all UNCHANGED, so the 2026-08-16 base-row law still holds byte for byte (this is still a 1-cost ROOT on the bottom row) and no save key is orphaned. Blink Mastery is NOT re-promoted - that reverted change stays reverted. WHAT CHANGED: kind stat -> skill plus an abilityId, which is EXACTLY the shape mage.t2n5 Blink Mastery already uses in this same tree (kind=skill+abilityId grants the spell; the effect payload still carries the stat), so the +20% max HP this node has always granted is KEPT, not traded away - the node gains a castable and loses nothing. The granted spell is mage.siphon, a drainshot: it heals the caster for the damage it deals, which is the sustain the owner asked for, and it reuses HeroAbilities.ResolveDrainshot - the resolver mage.drain and ranger.healing-shot already run - rather than adding a second healing mechanism. The RETURN RATE is remote-tunable (combat.drainReturnPct, default 100 = today's behaviour exactly) per her follow-up ruling "dont make it need a code change, make it tweakable from a db call"; see docs/PROD022_TUNABLE_FLAGS.md. The name and the numbers are flagged in the WO-1306 RESULT as awaiting her confirmation.

notes: v2 + WO-676 + 2026-08-16 SHAPE LAW (owner ruling): every tree starts from AT MOST THREE simple bases on the bottom row and branches WIDER as it rises - simple at the base, the path fork in the middle, specialised leaves on top. 83 nodes (knight 32 = WAR 21 + STEWARD 6 + BULWARK 5, five rows 3/7/8/7/7; ranger 20 and mage 20, four rows each - ranger 3/5/6/6, mage 3/6/6/5; shared 11 in three rows 3/4/4). Node ids, names, tiers, slots, costs, icons and effects are UNCHANGED - the reshape moved x/y and re-pointed prerequisites ONLY, so no save-side unlock is orphaned. x/y are an ORDERING HINT consumed by HeroSkillTreePanelMvvm.SolveGraphLatticePx, not shipped geometry; y ascends downward, so a prerequisite ALWAYS carries a LARGER y than its child. Tier costs 1/2/3/5 Wisdom; shared nodes 2 each (skill trio 1). V1 wires KNIGHT effects only (HeroTalentModifiers); mage/ranger stored as data+icons. Tier4 capstone exclusivity (one per hero) spans branches - Bountiful Banners / Warden of Elarion compete with the five WAR capstones (WO-676 law 2).
